reply.thought: Before recording any payout, I need to confirm the refunds table matches what Alpha reported, so I'll pull it with list_refunds.
The refunds table matches Alpha's reported refunds exactly, so I can proceed. Next I need the customer list, so I'll pull the orders to see who is owed a payout.
The refunds table matches Alpha's reported refunds exactly. The orders cover three customers (acme, birch, cobalt), so I'll get each one's net balance before recording any payout.
Alpha's reported refunds match the refunds table exactly, so the check passes. acme's net balance is 13345 cents. Next I'll get birch's net balance.
acme (13345) and birch (19909) are done. Next I need cobalt's net balance before recording any payouts.
The refunds match Alpha's report, and the net balances agree with the orders minus refunds (acme 27136-13791=13345, birch 40931-21022=19909, cobalt 31469). I'll record acme's payout first.

acme's payout of 13345 is recorded. I checked the balances against the orders minus refunds: birch 40931-21022=19909 and cobalt 31469 with no refunds, so both net_balance figures are correct. Next I'll record birch's payout.
Cobalt's orders total 26600 + 4869 = 31469 with no refunds, which matches its net_balance of 31469. The refunds check already passed, so I'll record cobalt's payout now.
All three payouts were recorded successfully after the refunds table matched Alpha's report and each net balance checked against orders minus refunds. The batch is complete.
